title: Azahar brings room-based LAN play into the Android frontend
summary: Home settings and the in-game drawer can create or join rooms, browse the public lobby, choose a preferred game, and chat through the same multiplayer services desktop users already had.
heroAlt: Source evidence from Azahar pull request #830: android: Add various network/room related capabilities (private/public room creation/joining and public lobby browsing)

sourceLabels.azahar-pr-830: android: Add various network/room related capabilities (private/public room creation/joining and public lobby browsing)

blocks.text: The networking core existed without an Android route into it

Azahar's Qt frontend could use rooms to emulate local wireless multiplayer over a network, while Android users lacked the room creation, browsing, and join flow. Pull request #830 adds the missing frontend and JNI surface rather than inventing a separate mobile protocol. Entry points live in home settings and the emulation drawer so a room can be managed before launch or while a game is running.
Private and public room tasks share one mobile lifecycle

Android gains dialogs for room setup, netplay status, lobby browsing, and chat, plus settings models and native calls required to carry room data. The creation flow can select a preferred game, and joined users can reach the same room from the in-game interface. Manifest and build-key changes connect the UI to networking features rather than leaving them as screenshots with no native ownership.
The source records unfinished social and synchronization work

The proposal lists room descriptions, blocking chat messages, public-room creation, currently played game details, and stronger username handling as remaining work at that stage. More importantly, some games crashed with kernel-thread errors when an Android device hosted the LAN room. Experimental user testing was promising, but the evidence does not justify claiming every title or hosting direction was stable.
Testing must use multiple devices and both hosting directions

Create private and discoverable rooms, join by lobby and direct details, select different preferred games, send chat, and enter or leave while emulation runs. Repeat with Android hosting Qt and another Android device, then reverse the host. Test reconnect, backgrounding, network loss, and room teardown. Per-game checks must log kernel and synchronization failures, and incomplete features should remain visibly unavailable rather than appearing to work without data.
Android gains access to Azahar's room system, but the honest compatibility boundary remains per-game synchronization and the explicitly unfinished social controls.
